reporting-org.narrative: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

description.narrative: A senior loan of up to EUR 15 million (the "Loan") to the City of Kharkiv (the " City") in Ukraine, to finance the acquisition of distributed, resilient heat and electricity generating assets to restore heat supply tor residential, public and other buildings in the wake of the critical damage to the City's largest combined heat and power plant (the "Project"). The Loan is part of a broader financing package, which also includes a EUR 17 million investment grant from the European Union ("EU"). Given war-triggered risks, the Loan will also benefit from a partial guarantee provided by the EU on the first loss risk cover basis. The Loan and the EU grant proceeds will finance the acquisition of up to 22 small and medium-sized natural gas-fired modular boiler houses along with cogeneration units as well as 5 small cogeneration units in existing boiler houses. The implementation of the Project will result in restoration of District Heating ("DH") services, which were disrupted in February 2026 following the critical damage sustained by the Kharkiv combined heat and power plant No. 5 ("CHP-5"). The total annual reduction in greenhouse gas emission from the Project is calculated at 19,091 tonnes of CO2e.
